reviews.review: 10/10 game, brutal and beautiful at the same time.

Compared to the first title, the graphics and art style have clearly improved, and the developers’ passion for the Warhammer 40K universe is evident throughout the game.

The single-player campaign is relatively short, consisting of five parts, but it is structured well enough to keep players engaged from start to finish. The presentation and visual effects are solid, and the brutal action of the Space Marines—set against the vast scale of a universe-spanning conflict—is more than enough to captivate players for a while.

At first, the combat can feel overwhelming. The mix of gunfire, explosions, monstrous roars, and the constant need to read enemy attack timings can create a chaotic sensory overload for new players. However, once the systems begin to click, the experience becomes far more satisfying.

The campaign also remains accessible thanks to two AI companions who assist you throughout the story. Because of this, players generally don’t need to worry too much about the difficulty during the main campaign.

True to the principle that a game should be easy to finish but difficult to master, the experience expands after completing the story mode. The game opens up with more than ten additional Operation maps, along with several multiplayer options, including PvP-style modes and survival-type challenges where players try to stay alive as long as possible.

Fans of the Warhammer universe may find themselves losing track of time as they dive deeper into this detailed world. Ultimately, this title feels like a valuable gift for dedicated Warhammer fans. Even players who knew little about the setting beforehand may find themselves drawn into its brutal and vast universe.

I would love to see more games from these developers set in this universe, perhaps focusing on other factions such as the Eldar or the Necrons. For now, though, I can only hope that one day we might see something like Fire Warrior 2 with this level of quality.
Very beautiful game, high intensity and so much fun

Looking through the achievements, only about 20% of players have reached max level on a gun, which only took me around 20 hours. I’d recommend giving the game a try if it seems like something you’d be into. There’s a lot of content, regular player updates, and cosmetics, but no pay-to-win stuff. It also has plenty of hardcore or more chill ways to play.
